name: refuse-union-grazing-domes
why: Two domes whose flat feet overlap by 0.36 mm, unioned onto a plate: the fuse returned a watertight solid with one dome missing (1643.64 mm³, 7 faces, where both give about 1687 and 8) and raised no alert. A planter saucer lost 19 of 48 such bumps, and a denser layout lost the dish. Every point of an input's faces must be inside or on the union; the refusal names the lost input and the fix. GCC on x86_64 keeps both domes (1687.24 mm³), which is the right part, so the case also passes when the whole part is built: 8 faces, within 0.5% of 1687.2. A part with a dome missing is 2.6% light and 7 faces, and still fails.
